observations: Photo 0 and 2 show the same used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly, still bolted to a portion of an engine block, sitting on bare concrete ground.
Wiring harness, sensors, and a corroded exhaust flange are attached to the unit; no identification plate or stamped part number is legible.
Blue paint-pen marks ('CA', 'RG') and a green dot are visible on the casing — these are yard sorting marks, not manufacturer data.
A semi-transparent watermark reading 'GEARUP INC.' overlays all three photos — this is the seller/poster's business branding, not a part brand.
Photo 1 shows a wider yard view with multiple engines/transmissions stacked together and a worker's leg in frame, suggesting a used-parts (tokunbo) yard rather than a single clean unit shot.
No VIN tag, casting number, or Jeep/Chrysler logo is readable in any photo.
No video or photo of the transmission being tested, rotated by hand, or fluid being checked.

identity.kind: used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly (seller claims fitment: Jeep Wrangler 3.6L, 2011-2017, 4x4)

claims.evidence: No part number, casting mark, or VIN tag is legible in photo 0, 1, or 2 to confirm vehicle application.
No shipping label, customs tag, or import documentation visible in any photo.
No odometer photo or mileage sticker shown; mileage cannot be read from a disassembled gearbox.

risks.risk: Internal condition (gears, clutch packs, torque converter, seals) could be worn or damaged despite clean external casing
risks.proof: Video of the transmission being manually rotated at the input/output shaft, or a bench spin test

risks.risk: Fitment to the specific Jeep Wrangler 3.6L trim/4x4 transfer case configuration cannot be confirmed without visible part number
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the casting/part number tag or OEM sticker on the case

risks.risk: Unit may have been sitting exposed outdoors (seen on wet/dirty concrete), risking rust ingress into seals, bearings or electrical connectors
risks.proof: Close-up of seals, connector pins, and output shaft surface condition

risks.risk: Risk of mix-up at the yard, since photo 1 shows many similar transmissions stacked together — the one shipped may differ from the one photographed
risks.proof: Photo of the unit with a unique tag or marking tied to the buyer's order, taken at dispatch
risks.if_unproven: priced with mismatch risk factored in

risks.risk: No confirmation of transmission type (automatic vs manual) or whether transfer case is included as one unit or separate
risks.proof: Wide shot showing full assembly boundaries and any shift lever/solenoid pack identifying automatic vs manual
risks.if_unproven: priced as base assembly only, no extras assumed

proof_requests: Close-up photo of any stamped part/casting number or OEM tag on the transmission case
Video of the input/output shaft being rotated by hand or a bench test showing gear engagement
Photo of the odometer or any documentation supporting 'low mileage' and 'Direct America' claims
Close-up of seals, connector pins, and mounting bolts for rust/wear assessment
A dispatch-time photo tying this specific unit (with its blue paint marks) to the buyer's shipment
response.reason: The photos clearly show a used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly, so it can be identified and priced by type, but none of the seller's fitment, origin, or condition claims can be confirmed from the images, so it must be priced at worst case pending the proofs listed.
